title: hivemind_find returns 0 results for every query despite 13 stored memories with embeddings
description:
hivemind_stats reports: memories 13, embeddings 13, healthy true, ollama_available true, all 13 chunks under collection "opencode-swarm". So storage is working.

But hivemind_find returns {"results": [], "count": 0} for EVERY query tried, including single-word queries that must match stored content: "moonrepo", "kata", "template", and "moon template tera interpolation kata bun". Workers in this epic explicitly stored moon/Tera/template learnings that these queries should hit.

Impact: this is severe and silent. Every swarm worker prompt mandates "query hivemind BEFORE writing any code". Workers run the query, get 0 results, correctly conclude "no prior art", and proceed — so the failure looks identical to a genuinely greenfield repo. The swarm's collective memory is write-only: it accumulates learnings that can never be retrieved, and every agent repeats work the previous one already did.

Timeline note: at the start of this epic Ollama was down and hivemind_store failed outright (a researcher reported two failed attempts). Ollama is up now and stores succeed. So embedding generation recovered, but retrieval did not — suggesting the issue is in the query/similarity path rather than the embedding path. Possible leads: memories written while Ollama was down may have null/zero-vector embeddings inflating the count; or a similarity threshold that filters everything; or a collection-scoping mismatch (all chunks are under "opencode-swarm" while find may default to "default").

Repro: hivemind_stats (shows 13/13 healthy) then hivemind_find(query="kata", limit=10) -> 0 results.

title: Migrate hivemind embeddings to MLX runner with nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (768-dim)
description:
NO-GO — verified by benchmark on M5 / 24GB, not inferred. Step 1 (katas--w5hg2-mshpacihhs2) closed with evidence:

1. nomic-embed-text-v1.5 has NO MLX build — verified against the HuggingFace API, not assumed. The entire rationale for that model (dual Ollama+MLX runtime enabling a clean A/B) evaporates. mlx-omni-server ended up running mlx-community/mxbai-embed-large-v1 — literally the same weights Ollama already serves.

2. No speed win. Warm median n=20: MLX 32.0ms vs Ollama 33.1ms. A wash.

3. RAM is WORSE: MLX resident ~1.26GB (fp32) vs Ollama ~686MB (F16 quantized).

4. Dependency bloat: "MLX-native" mlx-omni-server pulled torch, spacy, transformers, jieba — a 1.7GB venv for a local embedding call.

5. Matryoshka truncation is not implemented server-side — the `dimensions` request param exists in the schema but is never used in the code. Dimension is fixed at 1024 (counted, not trusted from docs).

THE ONE REAL FINDING: MLX cold start 366ms vs Ollama 7.96s. That gap is Ollama's idle model-unload, NOT an inherent MLX advantage — fixable with OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE. That is a one-line env change instead of a provider shim + schema migration F32_BLOB(1024)->768 + full re-embed + a second hand-patch of the 440K-line plugin bundle.

RECOMMENDATION: abandon the MLX swap, set OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE to keep mxbai-embed-large resident. Same benefit, none of the risk. Child steps 2 (katas--w5hg2-mshpafx6fq5) and 3 (katas--w5hg2-mshpah25r05) should be closed unless the user wants MLX for reasons beyond efficiency.

title: swarm.db has no single-writer arbitration — every tool call opens a fresh SQLite connection, causing SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY under concurrent swarms
description:
ROOT CAUSE of three swarm.db wipes on 2026-08-06 (last one 15:53, ~536KB empty-tables file, memories:0 embeddings:0 healthy:true).

ARCHITECTURE: hivemind_*/hive_* MCP tools shell out to the `swarm` CLI binary (~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/opencode-swarm-plugin/dist/bin/swarm.js) per invocation — every single tool call is a brand-new OS process that opens its own @libsql/client connection directly against the local WAL-mode file ~/.config/swarm-tools/swarm.db, does its work, and closes. There is no long-lived daemon/server holding a stable lock or serializing writes across concurrent agents.

EVIDENCE:
- logs/errors-2026-08-06.log shows SQLITE_BUSY and SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY on hive_close/hive_sync/hivemind_stats repeatedly across the whole afternoon (14:59, 15:42, 16:04, 16:59, 19:50), spanning well before and after the 15:53 wipe — this is a persistent, ongoing condition, not a one-off.
- SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY specifically means a connection found a hot/inconsistent WAL and couldn't complete recovery because another process held a conflicting lock — i.e., WAL recovery was actively contending, repeatedly, all day.
- Reproduced live during this recovery session: a single sequential hivemind_store() followed immediately by hivemind_find() (no other agents running, verified via `ps aux`) hit SQLITE_BUSY on the very next call. This is NOT purely a multi-agent problem — the per-call connection churn alone is enough to race the WAL/shm state.
- The last logged tool_call before the 15:53 wipe was hive_create at 15:52:04; nothing is logged again until 16:04:23. Whatever wrote empty tables to swarm.db during that gap did not go through the logged CLI tool-call path — consistent with a WAL checkpoint/recovery event resolving to an empty/stale snapshot rather than an explicit DROP TABLE.
- RULED OUT: dropLibSQLMemorySchema()/validateLibSQLMemorySchema() exist in the bundle (grep confirmed, dist/bin/swarm.js:11391) but are only ever invoked from unit tests in the source tree (schema-overhaul.test.ts, libsql-schema.test.ts, entity-extraction.test.ts) — never from any production code path in the CLI. Not the mechanism.
- RULED OUT: no cron/launchd job touches swarm.db (checked crontab -l and ~/Library/LaunchAgents). No swarm/libsql process was running at investigation time (safe window confirmed).
- RULED OUT: the status-corruption hand-patch work (upstream-patches/swarm-tools-hivemind-status-fix, applied ~15:17) explicitly did NOT touch the live global install or swarm.db per its own README — all work happened in scratch clones.

MECHANISM (best-supported hypothesis): many short-lived processes opening/closing WAL-mode SQLite connections against the same local file, with implicit auto-checkpoints racing live writers from other just-spawned processes, occasionally causes a checkpoint/recovery to complete against a truncated or stale page set — silently emptying tables while leaving schema intact (exactly the observed symptom: healthy:true, 0 rows, tables present).

PREVENTION (recommended, priority order):
1. Route all local swarm.db access through a single long-lived process (e.g. a local libSQL server / sqld, or an in-process singleton connection pool inside a persistent MCP server) instead of CLI-per-tool-call. This is the actual fix — everything else is mitigation.
2. If (1) isn't immediately feasible: set `PRAGMA busy_timeout` high (10000ms+) on every connection the CLI opens, and wrap every write path in retry-with-backoff on SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY (purge-garbage.ts already does this — the pattern should move into the shared CLI DB-open path, not stay script-local).
3. Add a scheduled (e.g. hourly, low-cost) automated backup rotation of swarm.db — the only reason this incident was recoverable three times is that manual/ad-hoc backups happened to exist. That should not be load-bearing.
4. Add a startup/periodic health check that does a real round-trip (store+find, not just stats) and alerts loudly on silent-empty state, since `healthy:true` with 0 rows is indistinguishable from "fresh install" today.

title: Upstream fix: status default corruption lives in opencode-swarm-plugin bundle, not swarm-mail
description:
Durable follow-up to katas--w5hg2-mshn7z19q79, which was fixed only by patching compiled output in the global install. That patch is silently reverted by the next `bun install -g`.

ROOT CAUSE: Drizzle schema `db/schema/memory.ts` ~line 86 has `status: text("status").default("'active'")` — the default value contains literal single-quote characters, so every memory is written with the 7-char string 'active' instead of the 6-char active. store() never sets status explicitly, so all rows inherit it. search() and ftsSearch() then filter `WHERE (m.status IS NULL OR m.status = 'active')`, which never matches. Result: every query returns 0 results while stats reports a healthy corpus. Silent and total.

CRITICAL DISCOVERY — the obvious fix target is WRONG: patching ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/swarm-mail had ZERO effect. The hivemind_* MCP tools shell out to the `swarm` CLI, which resolves to ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/opencode-swarm-plugin/dist/bin/swarm.js — a separate, independently-bundled ~440K-line copy of the same swarm-mail logic. The plugin VENDORS its own copy. This was found only by testing store->find end-to-end and watching a brand-new memory get corrupted again after the first patch appeared to succeed. Any upstream fix that only touches swarm-mail will appear to work in isolation and change nothing in practice.

The bundle contained multiple copies: 1 schema default + 4 statusFilter occurrences (2 pairs from duplicate bundling) + 1 additional schema default in a third bundled copy. A fix must sweep all of them, or fix the source and rebuild the plugin bundle.

SCOPE OF DAMAGE: any memory written by any unpatched install is unreachable. The fix should (a) correct the schema default so new writes are clean, AND (b) widen the status filter to also accept the legacy corrupted value so previously-written rows stay searchable. Both. (b) alone leaves the corruption ongoing; (a) alone orphans existing memories.

Existing memories are fully recoverable with a metadata UPDATE — no re-embedding needed, embeddings are valid.

Source checkout at ~/.opencode-autopsy/joelhooks/swarm-tools has a partial fix (widened statusFilter + ANN-fallback exact scan) that was NEVER PUBLISHED — its package.json version 1.11.2 is identical to what npm serves and what is installed, so there is no version signal that a fix exists. The schema default is still wrong even there.

title: hivemind sync non-idempotent: id-only dedup causes content duplication on rehydrate+sync
description:
Root cause: `syncMemories()` (packages/swarm-mail/src/memory/sync.ts) does import-then-export against .hive/memories.jsonl. `importSingleMemory()` dedupes strictly by exact `id` match (SELECT id FROM memories WHERE id = $1) — never by content hash. Meanwhile `hivemind_store`/the adapter's insert path (packages/swarm-mail/src/memory/adapter.ts:360) mints a fresh id every call via `mem-${randomBytes(8).toString("hex")}`.

Reproduced sequence (2026-08-06/07, swarm.db):
1. 14 memories existed with original ids (created ~14:34-15:47 on 08-06), git-synced to .hive/memories.jsonl.
2. A DB wipe/embedding-loss event occurred (see swarm.db.bak_wiped_20260806_155458).
3. A rehydration worker restored the 14 memories via hivemind_store (or equivalent), which minted 14 NEW random ids + fresh embeddings (inserted 02:49-02:50 on 08-07).
4. A subsequent hivemind_sync/hive_sync ran importMemories() against the still git-tracked JSONL, which contained the ORIGINAL 14 ids. Since those ids didn't exist in the DB (the rehydration path never preserved them), the id-only existence check found nothing to skip and INSERTed all 14 as new rows — same content, no embedding, updated_at falling back to DEFAULT(datetime('now')), which is why all 14 duplicate rows share the exact same updated_at timestamp.
5. syncMemories()'s export step then dumped ALL 28 rows (14 original + 14 duplicate) back into .hive/memories.jsonl, permanently poisoning the git-tracked file.

Impact: any recovery/rehydration flow that doesn't explicitly preserve original memory ids will silently duplicate content on the very next sync, and that duplication gets written back to git — it recurs indefinitely until someone manually dedupes both the DB and the JSONL.

Fix direction: dedupe on import by content hash (or normalized content), not id alone; or make rehydration/recovery tooling always preserve original JSONL ids when re-inserting recovered content.

Note: .hive/memories.jsonl in the katas repo is currently polluted with 28 entries (both original and duplicate ids) as a result of this bug. It was NOT touched as part of this cleanup (constraint: do not touch the katas repo) — it will need a follow-up fix or the next sync will re-duplicate the DB again.

title: swarm-mail tests wipe/mutate shared production swarm.db (no SWARM_DB_PATH isolation)
description:
Discovered while fixing katas--w5hg2-msid02p0mpo (memory sync idempotency).

`getDatabasePath()` in packages/swarm-mail/src/streams/index.ts always resolves to the single global `~/.config/swarm-tools/swarm.db` (by design — "local DBs are banned") unless `process.env.SWARM_DB_PATH` is set.

None of the swarm-mail test files that call `getSwarmMailLibSQL()` / `getDatabasePath()` (libsql.convenience.test.ts, streams/index.test.ts, streams/store-auto-adapter.test.ts, streams/swarm-mail.test.ts, streams/events.test.ts) set `SWARM_DB_PATH` for isolation. Running `bun test` in packages/swarm-mail therefore opens real connections against, and can mutate/wipe, the live shared production database that every project's hivemind/CASS memory system depends on.

Reproduced twice in one session: running the swarm-mail test suite (`bun test`, full 1352-test run) coincided with the live `~/.config/swarm-tools/swarm.db` memories table dropping from 14 rows to 0 rows, both times. Confirmed via direct @libsql/client inspection (COUNT(id), not the vector-index-broken COUNT(*) via stock sqlite3) before and after.

This is likely also a contributing/alternate explanation for earlier "swarm.db wipe" reports beyond the WAL-truncate bug fixed in 0be039e — any local dev or CI run of `bun test` for swarm-mail is a live foot-gun against the shared global memory corpus.

Fix: every test file that calls getSwarmMailLibSQL/getDatabasePath without an explicit override should set `process.env.SWARM_DB_PATH` to a per-test tmpdir path in beforeAll/beforeEach, restoring it in afterAll/afterEach. Consider also adding a guard in getDatabasePath() (or a test-only assertion) that throws if called under `bun test`/NODE_ENV=test without SWARM_DB_PATH set, to make this fail loudly instead of silently corrupting production data.

title: Maintain srmcguirt/swarm-tools as a divergent fork with our own fixes
description:
User decision: stop hand-patching the global install and instead run from a maintained fork. Upstream appears stale (PR #206 has no maintainer engagement, CI stuck at action_required pending first-time-contributor approval).

RATIONALE: every fix so far is a patch to compiled output in ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/opencode-swarm-plugin/dist/bin/swarm.js, silently reverted by the next `bun install -g`. This tooling is load-bearing for daily work and is broken in several significant ways. Running from a fork makes fixes persist.

[... Milestones 1-4 unchanged, see prior description in git history ...]

=== MILESTONE 5 COMPLETE (2026-08-07, Phase 3 - rebuild/reinstall/purge, run solo) ===

STEP 1 - REBUILD/REINSTALL: Confirmed the previously-packed tarballs (built Aug 6 23:09) predated the branch HEAD commit 40349dd (2026-08-07 09:32:10) - start_time was still required in that stale build. Rebuilt clean in dependency order (swarm-queue -> swarm-mail -> opencode-swarm-plugin), packed fresh tarballs, backed up the global install (tar.gz + recorded old md5s: index.js ee8e9184b609d87430536437c9a9178a, plugin.js e8c5a237717988420949b472172c6650), reinstalled swarm-mail then opencode-swarm-plugin globally. New md5s (index.js 6b5b50664395bfe2ccdaa2a1cf456d08, plugin.js 414a38025d4ce8973d3a3d6ed860fa94) differ from backup, confirming a real swap. All 6 fixes verified present in the freshly installed dist via grep (start_time optional, insight tools registered x10, default("active") clean with zero corrupted-quote occurrences, existingByContent dedup, WAL checkpoint only in close()/checkpoint() not on every open). `swarm doctor` reports healthy. Rollback: `bun remove -g opencode-swarm-plugin swarm-mail && bun add -g opencode-swarm-plugin@0.63.2`.

STEP 2 - MCP HOST RESTART: Traced the bash tool's own process ancestry and confirmed my shell is a direct child of the opencode server process (PID 3649, port 3456) serving this session - i.e. I run inside the exact host the task warned was "long-running and caches loaded code." Could not kill/restart that process without terminating my own execution. However, live acceptance testing against that unrestarted process showed the fix was ALREADY active: `swarm_complete` succeeded without start_time, and all three insight tools (`swarm_get_strategy_insights`, `swarm_get_pattern_insights`, `swarm_get_file_insights`) returned real results, not "Unknown tool." No spawn/exec/child_process calls were found wrapping these specific tools in the bundled index.js, so this isn't a CLI-subprocess-per-call architecture; the most likely explanation is that opencode reloads plugin modules fresh per new session/conversation rather than caching for the lifetime of the server process. Documented for the user: sessions that were ALREADY OPEN before this reinstall may still be serving stale cached code and would need a fresh session (not necessarily a full server kill) to pick up the rebuild - this could not be verified for other concurrent sessions from within this one.

STEP 3 - DB PURGE (used @libsql/client throughout, never stock sqlite3): Backed up ~/.config/swarm-tools/swarm.db (+wal/+shm) to a new timestamped file before touching anything; verified sizes matched. Confirmed FTS5 has proper AFTER INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE triggers and the vector index (idx_memories_embedding, libsql_vector_idx) is natively maintained, so a scoped DELETE keeps both consistent without manual shadow-table surgery. Matched all 4646 memories rows against the 14-entry .hive/memories.jsonl by exact content (not id) - all 14 canonical entries matched 1:1 by both content AND id, zero ambiguity, zero missing. Deleted the other 4632 rows: memories 4646 -> 14, memories_fts 14, embeddings 14 (all 14 keepers had embeddings pre-purge). For beads: confirmed FK CASCADE + `PRAGMA foreign_keys=1` already correct, so a single scoped DELETE was safe. Found exactly 2 non-scratch project_keys among 174 total (everything else was /tmp/* or /var/folders/*/T/* test fixture paths with timestamps in the names, e.g. tool-adapter-*, test-swarm-complete-*, hive-*-test-*): katas (8 beads, kept) and swarm-tools/packages/opencode-swarm-plugin (120 beads - sampled titles confirmed real historical work like "Pino Logging Infrastructure," "Fix SQL injection in cursor.ts," left untouched as real, non-scratch project history). Deleted 568 beads across 172 scratch project_keys: 696 -> 128. Verified zero orphans in bead_comments/bead_dependencies (both FK columns)/bead_labels/blocked_beads_cache/dirty_beads after cascade. Checkpointed WAL after each mutation.

STEP 4 - VERIFICATION: hivemind_stats = 14 memories / 14 embeddings. hivemind_find("moon template tera interpolation kata bun") returned the exact baseline top-5 scores (0.72286/0.69739/0.65935/0.65068/0.65052 vs baseline 0.7229/0.6974/0.6593/0.6507/0.6505), no duplicates. hivemind_find("kata") returned 10 non-zero, no-duplicate results. store->find->remove round trip via hivemind_* tools (tool-level path, not raw SQL) worked cleanly and left the corpus at 14/14. Two consecutive hive_sync runs both left memories at 14/14 and .hive/memories.jsonl at 14 lines with zero new commits (git status clean both times) - true idempotency, not just "didn't crash." hive_cells now shows only real work: the 8 katas cells plus a summary note for the other legitimate project (opencode-swarm-plugin, 120 cells) - zero scratch project keys visible. Re-checked hivemind_stats after a 20s pause: still 14/14, nothing regrew.

EVERYTHING STILL LIVE PER THE SIX FIXES: confirmed via both static grep of the freshly built dist AND live runtime behavior in this session. Nothing reverted, nothing skipped.

katas repo untouched throughout (constraint honored - .hive/memories.jsonl was already correct at 14 entries and stayed that way). No test suites run this task. No force-push, no touching of PR #206 or fix/memory-status-default-quotes, no push to joelhooks/swarm-tools. All prior DB backups preserved (6 in ~/.config/swarm-tools/backups/, none overwritten).

This closes out the fork-maintenance epic: fixes are built, installed, verified live, and the production memory/cell corpus is clean.

title: Documentation service: structured, styled, auto-generating docs from project progress
description:
Build a portable documentation service that reads hive data (cells, memories, outcomes) plus git history and generates + MAINTAINS a structured documentation set. Must work across any project or company, not be welded to one repo's shape.

CORE IDEA: structured, styled, auto-generating based on project progress. Not one-shot generation — it stands these functions up and keeps them current as work lands.

FOUR OUTPUT TYPES:
1. RUNBOOKS — operational procedures for running the project. Source: verified procedures captured in cell closure notes. Real examples from this session: build order (swarm-queue -> swarm-mail -> opencode-swarm-plugin, because their `main` points at dist/); global reinstall flow (bun pm pack -> bun remove -g -> bun add -g, and that `bun pm pack` does NOT bundle workspace:* deps); rollback commands; DB backup-before-migrate procedure.
2. WIKI + DOC SITE — plain language explanation plus code docs. Diataxis (tutorial/how-to/reference/explanation). Styled via tastemaker.
3. BLOG — narrative for epic arcs: timeline, what happened, what was learned. Source material from this session is unusually strong: three independent DB destroyers with measured root causes, an embedding migration rejected on benchmark evidence, a bug found and PR'd to a public package.
4. POLICY — hardline rules derived from incidents. Examples earned today: never use stock sqlite3 against a libSQL DB (bare COUNT(*) silently returns 0 via an unusable vector index); never run `bun test` from repo root (skips the bunfig.toml SWARM_DB_PATH preload); always back up before schema migration; verify a fix is LIVE, not just committed (a stale MCP host served pre-fix code and polluted the DB during the very task that fixed it).

CROSS-CUTTING: everything emitted must pass the external-code sanitization policy — GitHub user as originator, no agent-identifying information, no AI-slop prose, no internal process vocabulary (swarm/worker/coordinator/cell/hive/subtask) in externally-visible artifacts. A generator fed by hive data is precisely where that vocabulary would leak into public docs, so the gate belongs inside the generator, not bolted on after.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS:
- Portable: project-agnostic config, droppable into any repo
- Idempotent regeneration; must not clobber hand-authored edits (generated-vs-authored marker)
- Drift detection when code moves ahead of docs
- Styling via tastemaker, not hand-rolled CSS
